slides.0.title: Red grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Franc
slides.1.title: Oregon: the Pinot Noir kingdom
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Six-tenths of the area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: In 2024 Pinot Noir was 60% of the state's planted area, far ahead of every other variety
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The Burgundy connection
slides.1.highlights.1.content: In 1987 the Drouhin family bought 100 acres in the North Willamette Valley and founded Domaine Drouhin Oregon
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The labelling threshold
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Oregon law requires at least 90% of a named variety on the label (with exceptions for some varieties, see L1-5)
slides.1.content: Oregon = Pinot Noir: six-tenths of the area, a Burgundian family's investment and a strict 90% labelling rule.
slides.2.title: Washington: led by Cabernet Sauvignon
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The top variety by crush
slides.2.highlights.0.content: In 2024 Cabernet Sauvignon was crushed at 40,589 tons, about 27% of the state's roughly 150,000-ton total
slides.2.highlights.1.title: More red than white
slides.2.highlights.1.content: In 2024 reds were 55% and whites 45%; the top seven varieties together made up 86%
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Syrah and Merlot
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Syrah is described as the fastest-growing red; Cabernet Sauvignon has overtaken Merlot, once the leader
slides.2.content: Washington is a continental region of both reds and whites, with Cabernet Sauvignon at a bit over a quarter of the crush.
slides.3.title: New York: Cabernet Franc and Merlot
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Cabernet Franc
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Named with Riesling as a signature New York vinifera; it ripens earlier, which suits the cool East Coast
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Merlot
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A common red on Long Island, where the first commercial vineyard and winery were established in 1973
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Style orientation
slides.3.highlights.2.content: East Coast reds tend to emphasise cool-climate acidity and finesse rather than concentration
slides.3.content: East Coast reds revolve around Cabernet Franc and Merlot in a cool, fine style.
